summary.short: Draft CAC rule, open for comment until 3 May 2026, for small personal information handlers processing fewer than 100,000 individuals' data. It simplifies notice, cross-border transfer, audit, impact assessment, breach notification and penalty mitigation duties under the PIPL; the effective date is left blank.
summary.long: The draft Provisions on Simplified Personal Information Protection Measures for Small Personal Information Handlers, published for comment by the Cyberspace Administration of China on 3 April 2026, applies within mainland China to handlers processing personal information of fewer than 100,000 individuals (Art. 2). Its stated aim is to ease Personal Information Protection Law duties for small and micro enterprises. Handlers may publish processing rules in simplified form (Art. 4), and park or property managers may publish unified rules for tenants (Art. 5). Notice of transfers on merger, split or dissolution may be given by posting or pop-up (Art. 9). Cross-border provision is exempt from security assessment, standard contract and certification in listed cases, such as contract performance, cross-border HR management, emergencies, legal duties, and cumulative transfers under 100,000 non-sensitive individuals a year (Art. 11). Compliance audits and impact assessments may use simplified forms at least every five years, with records kept (Arts. 14–15). Breach notice may be posted where direct notice is impossible (Art. 17). Certified handlers may skip audits during certification validity (Art. 18). No or reduced penalties apply in listed circumstances (Arts. 19–20). The effective date is left blank (Art. 22).

notes: Consultation draft (征求意见稿) with the comment period ending 2026年5月3日 per the cover notice. Art. 22 leaves the effective date blank (自 年 月 日起施行), so no commencement date is stated. The annex forms referred to in Arts. 14 and 15 (compliance audit self-check form, impact assessment form) are not part of the fetched text. Art. 8 uses 网络平台 without defining it. Art. 11(5) sets a cumulative cross-border cut-off of fewer than 100,000 persons counted from 1 January, a different measure from the Art. 2 small-processor definition of fewer than 100,000 persons handled. Target instrument IDs are empty because no registry IDs were available for the cited laws.

thresholds.consequence: Exempt from declaring a data export security assessment, concluding a standard contract, and obtaining personal information protection certification for the cross-border provision.
thresholds.conditions: Handler is not a critical information infrastructure operator; the provision covers only personal information provided abroad, excluding sensitive personal information and important data.
